title: Just one word
q: Pixar films with a one-word title
rule: Pixar features released through 2026. The printed title must be one word, so a leading 'The' or a sequel number rules a film out; a hyphenated title counts as one word.
fact: Only one of these twelve titles is an acronym: WALL-E, short for Waste Allocation Load Lifter: Earth-Class.

traps.Incredibles: The film is 'The Incredibles', two words.
traps.Cars 2: Add the sequel number and it's no longer one word.
traps.Frozen: That's Disney Animation Studios, not Pixar.

title: Shaken, one word
q: James Bond films with a one-word title
rule: The 25 Eon Productions films, Dr. No (1962) to No Time to Die (2021). The title must be one word as printed; 'Dr. No' is two.
fact: GoldenEye is named after Ian Fleming's Jamaican estate, where he wrote the Bond novels.

traps.Never Say Never Again: Not an Eon film, and four words.

title: Count the clues
q: Agatha Christie novels with a number in the title
rule: Judged on the current UK title, with a cardinal number as digits or a word (zero counts). Ordinals like 'Third' don't, and neither do short-story collections or US-only titles.
fact: Two of these titles are nursery rhymes, and US editions renamed both: Five Little Pigs became Murder in Retrospect, and One, Two, Buckle My Shoe became The Patriotic Murders.

traps.Third Girl: 'Third' is an ordinal, not a number.
traps.The Thirteen Problems: A short-story collection, not a novel.
traps.Thirteen at Dinner: A US title; the UK title, Lord Edgware Dies, has no number.

title: Name tag
q: Disney animated classics titled with just the hero's name
rule: Walt Disney Animation Studios canon only, so no Pixar. The whole title must be the hero's name or nickname; numbered sequels don't count.
fact: Pocahontas (1995) was Disney's first animated feature based on a real historical figure.

traps.Snow White: The full title is Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
traps.Sleeping Beauty: That's a description; the heroine's name is Aurora.
traps.Luca: That's Pixar, not Disney Animation Studios.

title: Not Hayao
q: Studio Ghibli films not directed by Hayao Miyazaki
rule: Any of Studio Ghibli's 25 features. The directing credit decides, so films Miyazaki only wrote or produced count, and so does Ghibli's European co-production.
fact: Hayao Miyazaki's son Gorō directed three of these films: Tales from Earthsea, From Up on Poppy Hill and Earwig and the Witch.

title: Her name was
q: Beatles album tracks with a woman's name in the title
rule: Songs from the 12 UK studio albums plus Magical Mystery Tour. A woman's name counts even when the song is about a pet; street names and terms of endearment don't.

head: Eleanor Rigby
Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds
Michelle

fact: Martha My Dear is about Paul McCartney's Old English sheepdog, and Sexy Sadie began life as a barb at the Maharishi.

traps.Lady Madonna: A standalone single, not on any of those albums.
traps.Penny Lane: Penny Lane is a Liverpool street, not a woman.
traps.Honey Pie: A pet name, not a given name.
traps.Hey Jude: Jude is a man, and it wasn't on a UK studio album.

title: Pass Go
q: Properties you can buy on the classic London Monopoly board
rule: The 28 buyable spaces on the classic UK board: 22 streets, 4 stations and 2 utilities. Themed, city and 'Here & Now' editions don't count.
fact: Bow Street, Marlborough Street and Vine Street, the orange set, each had a magistrates' court or police station.

traps.Baker Street: Famous, but not on the board.
traps.Paddington: The four stations are King's Cross, Marylebone, Fenchurch Street and Liverpool Street.

title: Soul searching
q: Voldemort's seven Horcruxes, made on purpose or by accident
rule: The seven vessels that held a piece of his soul in the novels. His own body doesn't count, and neither do the Deathly Hallows.
fact: Voldemort meant to make six Horcruxes, but he made a seventh by accident in Harry on the night he failed to kill him.

traps.Elder Wand: A Deathly Hallow, not a Horcrux.
traps.Resurrection Stone: It was set in the Gaunt ring; the ring was the Horcrux, not the stone.
traps.Invisibility Cloak: A Deathly Hallow, not a Horcrux.
traps.Sword of Gryffindor: It destroyed Horcruxes rather than being one.
traps.Voldemort: His own body held the main part of his soul, so it isn't a Horcrux.

title: King of Pop
q: The nine tracks on Michael Jackson's best-selling 1982 album
rule: The original album track list only. Bonus tracks on reissues and songs from his other albums don't count.
fact: Seven of Thriller's nine tracks were released as singles and all seven reached the US top ten, a first for any album.

traps.Say Say Say: A McCartney duet, but from Paul's Pipes of Peace (1983).

title: Set in stone
q: Original 151 Pokémon you get by using an evolution stone
rule: The evolved Pokémon you end up with after a Fire, Water, Thunder, Leaf or Moon Stone in Red, Blue and Yellow. Trade evolutions and the pre-evolved forms don't count.
fact: In Red and Blue, Eevee is the only Pokémon that evolves with more than one kind of stone: Water, Thunder or Fire for Vaporeon, Jolteon or Flareon.

traps.Pikachu: Pikachu is the Pokémon you use the stone on; it becomes Raichu.
traps.Eevee: Eevee is the Pokémon you use the stone on, not the result.
traps.Alakazam: Evolves by trade, not a stone.
traps.Gengar: Evolves by trade, not a stone.
traps.Golem: Evolves by trade, not a stone.

title: Unexpected party
q: The thirteen dwarves who set out with Bilbo in The Hobbit
rule: Their leader counts. Only the thirteen who set out from Bag End; dwarves met later, like Dáin, don't.
fact: Tolkien took the names of most of Thorin's company, and Gandalf's too, from a list of dwarves in the Old Norse poem Völuspá.

traps.Gimli: Glóin's son, but he's in The Lord of the Rings, not Thorin's company.
traps.Dáin Ironfoot: Thorin's cousin, who only arrives for the Battle of Five Armies.
traps.Thráin: Thorin's father, long gone by the time of the quest.
traps.Bilbo Baggins: A hobbit, the fourteenth member of the party.

title: Bend the knee
q: The nine Great Houses of Westeros in Game of Thrones
rule: The Great Houses as they stand at the start of the first book, counting the deposed royal house. Later risers like Bolton and Frey don't count.
fact: House Tully, lords of Riverrun, has a leaping trout for its sigil and 'Family, Duty, Honor' as its words.

traps.Bolton: Stark bannermen who only rose after the war began.
traps.Frey: Lords of the Crossing, not a Great House at the start.
traps.Mormont: A minor Northern house, sworn to the Starks.
traps.Hightower: Bannermen of the Tyrells in the main story.
traps.Velaryon: A Targaryen-kin house from House of the Dragon, not a Great House.

title: Family tree
q: The Simpson household plus the children's four grandparents, by first name
rule: The five who live at 742 Evergreen Terrace and their four grandparents. Aunts, half-siblings and neighbours don't count.
fact: Clancy Bouvier, Marge's father, is so rarely seen that most of his screen time is in flashbacks to Marge's childhood.

traps.Patty: Marge's sister, an aunt rather than a parent.
traps.Selma: Marge's sister, an aunt rather than a parent.

title: Skywalker saga
q: Films in the nine-part main saga about the Skywalker family
rule: The nine numbered episodes only: Solo, Rogue One and the animated spin-offs don't count.
fact: The 1977 original was released as just Star Wars; the subtitle A New Hope came later.

traps.Solo: Solo: A Star Wars Story (2018) is a standalone spin-off.
traps.Rogue One: Rogue One (2016) is a standalone spin-off.
traps.The Clone Wars: The 2008 animated film is a spin-off, not one of the nine.

title: Fab Four, plus
q: Musicians who were in the Beatles, from the early years to the end
rule: The Fab Four, the bassist and drummer who left before fame, and the drummer who stood in on the 1964 world tour.
fact: Jimmy Nicol deputised for Ringo Starr on a 1964 tour when Ringo was ill with tonsillitis.

traps.Billy Preston: Played with them on the late recordings but was never a member.
traps.George Martin: Their producer, often called the fifth Beatle.

title: Live forever
q: Oasis studio albums
rule: Studio albums only, so compilations and live albums don't count.

head: Definitely Maybe
(What's the Story) Morning Glory?
tail: Standing on the Shoulder of Giants

fact: Dig Out Your Soul (2008) was Oasis's last studio album before the band split in 2009.

traps.Stop the Clocks: A 2002 compilation, not a studio album.
traps.Familiar to Millions: A 2000 live album, not a studio album.

title: Through the back
q: Titles in C. S. Lewis's Chronicles of Narnia
rule: Book titles only, and a leading 'The' can be dropped.

head: Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe

fact: The Magician's Nephew tells Narnia's creation story but was published sixth, in 1955.

traps.The Hobbit: Tolkien's book, not part of Narnia.
traps.Charlie and the Chocolate Factory: A Roald Dahl novel, not Lewis.

title: Gobblefunk
q: Roald Dahl's children's stories in prose, by title
rule: His prose books for children, long or short. Memoirs, verse collections and adult short stories don't count.

head: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
Matilda
BFG
tail: Danny the Champion of the World
Charlie and the Great Glass Elevator
deep: Giraffe and the Pelly and Me

fact: The Gremlins (1943), written for Disney while he was an RAF officer, was Dahl's first children's book.

title: Nine walkers
q: Members of the Fellowship of the Ring
rule: All nine members count, including the wizard; Bilbo and Elrond don't.
fact: Gimli is the only dwarf in the Fellowship, and Legolas is the only elf.

traps.Bilbo Baggins: He stays behind at Rivendell, so he isn't a member.
traps.Saruman: The wizard never joins the Fellowship.
traps.Elrond: He holds the council but doesn't travel with the Fellowship.

title: Guest list
q: Characters in the classic board game Cluedo
rule: The six suspects and the murder victim from the classic British edition; their US names count too.
fact: Cluedo's US name is Clue, and Reverend Green is called Mr Green there.

traps.Miss Marple: Agatha Christie's detective, not a Cluedo suspect.

title: Room service
q: Rooms of the mansion on the Cluedo board
rule: The nine named rooms only; corridors and the central area don't count.
fact: Four corner rooms have secret passages: Kitchen to Study, and Conservatory to Lounge.

traps.Drawing Room: A real room type, but not on the Cluedo board.
traps.Bedroom: There is no bedroom on the Cluedo board.

title: Honey pot
q: Residents of the Hundred Acre Wood in A. A. Milne's books
rule: Characters from Milne's two books about the bear who live in the forest. Characters added by Disney don't count, and Heffalumps and Woozles are only imagined.
fact: Small, one of Rabbit's friends and relations, is also called Alexander Beetle; the whole wood goes looking for him in one story.

traps.Gopher: A Disney addition, not in Milne's books.
traps.Toad: From The Wind in the Willows, not the Hundred Acre Wood.

title: Final girl
q: Films in the main series that began in 1979, by title
rule: Crossovers with other franchises and TV series don't count.
fact: Alien 3 (1992) opens by killing off Newt and Hicks, the survivors of Aliens.

traps.Alien vs. Predator: A crossover, excluded by the rule.
traps.Alien: Earth: A TV series, not a film.

title: Clever girl
q: Films in the main Jurassic dinosaur series
rule: Cinema films only, so the TV series and theme-park rides don't count.
fact: Steven Spielberg directed Jurassic Park and The Lost World, but no later film in the series.

traps.Jurassic Park IV: No such film; the fourth was titled Jurassic World.
traps.Congo: A 1995 Michael Crichton adaptation, not part of this series.

title: Three sisters
q: Novels written by the Brontë sisters
rule: Full-length novels only; poetry and short fiction don't count.
fact: Charlotte's The Professor was rejected by publishers and only appeared in 1857, after her death.

traps.Mansfield Park: A Jane Austen novel, not a Brontë.

title: Wessex
q: Novels by Thomas Hardy
rule: Full-length novels only; short stories and poems don't count.
fact: Critics dubbed Jude the Obscure 'Jude the Obscene' because of its frank treatment of marriage.

traps.Middlemarch: A George Eliot novel, not Hardy.
traps.Wessex: Hardy's fictional region, not a novel.

title: Licence to play
q: Actors who played 007 on screen before 2006
rule: The leading Bond in any film or TV production; the actor whose first Bond film came in 2006 is out.
fact: Barry Nelson played an American Bond, called Jimmy Bond, in a 1954 US TV version of Casino Royale.

traps.Daniel Craig: His first Bond film came in 2006, outside the cut-off.
traps.Ralph Fiennes: He plays M, Bond's boss, not 007.

title: Song two
q: Studio albums by the Britpop band fronted by Damon Albarn
rule: Studio albums only; compilations, live albums and singles don't count.
fact: The Ballad of Darren (2023) was Blur's first album in eight years.

traps.Blur: The Best Of: A compilation, not a studio album.

title: Sorting hat
q: The four Hogwarts houses, or their founders' first names
rule: House names count, and so do the founders' first names; founders' surnames match the house names.
fact: Godric Gryffindor's sword was hidden in the Sorting Hat, and Harry used it to kill the basilisk.

traps.Dumbledore: Headmaster of Hogwarts, not a founder.
traps.Merlin: A legendary wizard, not a Hogwarts founder.
